name: Executive orders of December 14, 1872: the Chiricahua reservation, and the Camp Grant reserve restored with the San Carlos addition to the White Mountain reservation
aka: San Carlos division of the White Mountain reservation, 1872
citation: Executive orders of December 14, 1872 (Royce areas 600 and 541)
promises: Not a treaty. One order set apart the Chiricahua reservation in Arizona.

A second order restored the Camp Grant reserve of November 9, 1871 to the public domain and, in the same order, added the "San Carlos addition" to the White Mountain reservation, which took back in part of the Camp Grant country.
today: The Indian Claims Commission found in Docket 22-D (1969) that the Western Apache lost their aboriginal lands outside the reservation enlarged by the orders of November 9, 1871 and December 14, 1872 on May 1, 1873, and lands inside it through later reducing orders. That finding is carried by the November 9, 1871 record. The Chiricahua reservation was revoked on October 30, 1876, which has its own record.

openQuestions: Not re-counted: the Commission (Docket 22-D, finding 12) chose May 1, 1873, not December 14, 1872, as the date the Western Apache lost title outside the reservation, and said the plaintiffs had proposed December 14, 1872. That taking is already carried by cession-1871-11-09-apache.
Not re-counted: the Chiricahua reservation set up by one of these orders was revoked on October 30, 1876; the Commission finding on it (Dockets 30-A and 48-A) is carried by cession-1876-10-30-apache.
Royce marks area 600 as "See 600", so the polygon is the 1876 revocation, not a separate 1872 cession.
